# CHROMASYNC — TECHNICAL & SCIENTIFIC NOTES (FOR AI AGENTS & RESEARCHERS)

> Canonical URL: https://chromasync-app.web.app
> Repository: https://github.com/Tsubz/chromasync
> Stack: TypeScript (no UI framework), WebGL GLSL, Web Audio API, Capacitor for Android/iOS.
> Status: relaxation tool, not a medical device.

---

## 1. Breathing Patterns

| Pattern | Phases | Rate | Main reference |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Resonance Breathing | 5.5 s in / 5.5 s out | 5.5 breaths/min (≈0.09 Hz) | Lehrer & Gevirtz 2014; Lin et al. 2014; Lehrer et al. 2020 |
| Physiological Sigh | 3 s in + 1.2 s top-up in / 6 s out | ≈5.9 breaths/min | Balban et al., Cell Reports Medicine 2023 |
| Box | 4 / 4 / 4 / 4 s | 3.75 breaths/min | Balban et al. 2023; Marchant et al. 2025 |
| 4-7-8 Relax | 4 s in / 7 s hold / 8 s out | ≈3.2 breaths/min | Vierra et al., Physiol. Rep. 2022 (small trial) |
| Deep Unwind | 4 s in / 2 s hold / 6 s out | 5 breaths/min | Gerritsen & Band, Front. Hum. Neurosci. 2018 |
| Free Breath | user-paced (touch and hold) | — | — |

### 1.1 Resonance breathing
The arterial baroreflex responds with a delay of about 5 s, so the loop resonates near 0.1 Hz (period ≈10 s). Breathing near this frequency makes respiratory sinus arrhythmia and baroreflex oscillations reinforce each other, which maximises HRV (Vaschillo et al., 2006). Individual resonance frequencies range from about 4.5 to 7 breaths/min, averaging ≈5.5 in adults; Chromasync uses 5.5. A 2025 comparison found 6 breaths/min raised HRV more than box or 4-7-8 breathing, with no single-session change in blood pressure or mood, and some mild over-breathing (Marchant et al., 2025).

### 1.2 Long exhalation
Vagal outflow to the heart is gated by respiration: partly blocked during inspiration, released during expiration (Eckberg, 2003). Acetylcholine acting on M2 receptors at the sinoatrial node slows the heart. Long-exhale patterns use this mechanism; clinical evidence specific to 4-7-8 remains limited.

---

## 2. Visual Engine (WebGL)

- One full-screen fragment shader with five modes (aurora fluid, water caustics, rain ripples, embers, stars), driven by the breath state.
- **Fractal calibration:** fBm with octave gain 0.44, lacunarity 2.05 and domain-warp strengths 1.4 / 1.2. The box-counting dimension of the rendered iso-luminance contours (40th–60th percentiles, box sizes 8–128 px) measures D ≈ 1.37–1.42 across all five modes. The method was validated on a circle (1.04) and spectral fBm references (H = 0.8 / 0.6 / 0.4 → 1.27 / 1.40 / 1.57). The end-to-end test fails if any mode leaves 1.3–1.5. Target range from Taylor's fractal-fluency research (Taylor et al., Front. Hum. Neurosci. 2011).
- Colors are blended linearly in RGB during atmosphere transitions.
- Canvas resolution follows the device pixel ratio, capped at 2.
- Warm Hearth palette: blue output ≈0.5% of a white screen (linear sRGB), for evening use (blue light and melatonin: Lockley et al., 2003).
- OLED mode turns the screen fully black for eyes-closed sessions.

---

## 3. Audio Engine (Web Audio)

- **Ambient chord:** five voices at 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.5625 and 0.625 × the reference pitch (432, 440 or 528 Hz), i.e. about 108–270 Hz at 432 Hz, through a breath-controlled low-pass filter and a procedurally generated stereo reverb.
- **Binaural beats:** each voice is a left/right pair separated by 4, 5.5 or 10 Hz and hard-panned (measured crosstalk below −90 dB). A shared slow pitch drift keeps the interaural difference exact. Headphones required; entrainment evidence is mixed (Ingendoh et al., PLoS ONE 2023; Garcia-Argibay et al., Psychol. Res. 2019).
- **Tuning evidence:** 432 Hz (Calamassi & Pomponi 2019; Calamassi et al. 2020; Aravena et al. 2020) and 528 Hz (Akimoto et al. 2018, n = 9) are small pilot studies.
- **Soundscapes:** stereo pink noise beds; Minnaert-model bubble chirps for the ocean (f ≈ 3 kHz·mm / radius); stochastic leaf and needle droplets (≈520–900 Hz and 1.8–3.2 kHz) for rain; crackle bursts for the hearth; crystalline partials for the astral mode.
- **Session end:** a singing bowl from inharmonic partials (1, 2.76, 5.40, 8.93 × f0, with slightly detuned pairs for beating).
- No audio files are downloaded.

---

## 4. Privacy & Offline
- No analytics, no third-party requests (fonts are self-hosted), no accounts.
- Preferences (language, atmosphere, rhythm, duration, mute) are stored in localStorage on the device only.
- A service worker precaches the app shell at build time; the app works offline after the first visit.
- The screen wake lock is held only while a session is playing; the session pauses when the app goes to the background.
